subject: MAP: acceptance signals, exit checks, and close cadence
messages:
From: Emily Nelson <emily.nelson@clearwellhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP request — evaluation checklist & timelines

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the product walkthrough last week — the team was impressed by the latency and the caching approach. We need a concrete mutual action plan so procurement, engineering, and clinical ops can sign off on a short pilot. High level asks from our side:

- A one-page MAP that lists acceptance tests, owners, and dates for the 6-week trial.
- Clear pass/fail criteria for model quality (medical-terminology concordance) and latency under our 95th percentile SLA.
- A short list of deliverables we need from Redwood (logs, audit trail, SOC2 evidence, data retention commitments).

Can you put together a draft MAP with responsible owners and the proposed close cadence? Procurement wants a contract redline window of 10 business days after we confirm acceptance criteria.

If helpful, I can loop Jason from procurement — he’ll want to see the timeline and the DocuSign expectations.

Best,
Emily Nelson
Head of Clinical Integrations
Clearwell Health

[attachment: example-poc-scenario.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emily Nelson <emily.nelson@clearwellhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP request — evaluation checklist & timelines

Hi Emily — thanks, glad the demo resonated. I’ve attached a first-draft MAP and a short acceptance-playbook. Key points up-front:

1) Acceptance signals (pass = all must be met):
   - Quality: clinical-term concordance >= 0.92 F1 on the provided 1k probe set (we'll run evaluation with your canonical examples).
   - Hallucination: documented hallucination incidents <= 0.5% per 1k prompts (manual review sample).
   - Latency: p95 latency < 250ms for single-turn inference at nominal traffic (up to 50 RPS).
   - Throughput: baseline sustained throughput of 300 tokens/s for the pilot model variant.

2) Exit gates (stop conditions):
   - Failure to meet any of the acceptance signals after two remediation sprints (2 weeks total) OR
   - Security/compliance items unresolved (audit logs or KMS integration not provisioned) by pilot week 4.

3) Acceptance tests (owners & dates in attached MAP_v1.xlsx):
   - Redwood: prepare a reproducible smoke test harness + test vectors (deliverable: eval-test-vectors.zip) — due Wed 2027-02-24.
   - Clearwell: provide canonical 1k probe set and target labels by Fri 2027-02-19.
   - Joint: run daily smoke runs for weeks 2–4; weekly sync to compare diffs and triage failures.

I’ve included a Drive link to the living MAP so we can update owners/targets in real time: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-EvalMAP

Attachments: MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet with line-item tasks), acceptance-playbook.md (short-runbook).

Next steps: can you confirm who on your team will be the engineering owner for test data? Procurement timeline noted — we’ll time the signature window to begin after acceptance criteria are agreed.

Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123
[attachment: MAP_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Nelson <emily.nelson@clearwellhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: acceptance signals, exit checks, and close cadence

Adding technical detail on acceptance tests and a couple of caveats so Emily has visibility. Short version: the targets above are achievable but depend on the model variant and the tokenization of the probe set. Details:

- Quality eval: we’ll run both exact-match and fuzzy-aware F1 (medical synonyms normalized). If Clearwell provides the canonical labels, Redwood will run the scoring and share the notebook and seed for reproducibility.
- Latency measurement: p95 measured at our edge + inside the VPC (when private deployment); the acceptance p95 < 250ms will be measured under the defined traffic pattern in the MAP (burst profile + steady-state).
- KV cache warmup: expectation is a 1–2 minute warmup; we’ll include warmup scripts in eval-test-vectors.zip.
- Fallback behavior: in case of degraded quality, the MAP includes an automatic fallback to the smaller, conservative model variant with deterministic responses; fallback will be logged and counted toward pass/fail thresholds.
- Observability: we’ll deliver token-level cost breakdown for the pilot and an error-rate dashboard.

Open items for the MAP spreadsheet:
- Which environment do you want us to run the pilot in — Redwood Hosted (fastest) or Dedicated (isolated)? This changes provisioning lead time (Hosted: 3 business days; Dedicated: 10 business days).
- Data handling: need confirmation of retention period and whether any prompts include PHI (affects on-prem options).

I attached a short-runbook excerpt with the smoke commands and a checklist of logging fields (request_id, model_variant, p95_latency, hallucination_flag).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
[attachment: eval-test-vectors.zip (application/zip)]

From: Emily Nelson <emily.nelson@clearwellhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jason Li <jason.li@clearwellhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: acceptance signals, exit checks, and close cadence

Thanks Marissa and Ben — this is very helpful and concrete. Quick answers from procurement/engineering:

- Clearwell will provide the canonical 1k probe set by EOD Fri 2027-02-19 (I’ll send via the Drive folder you shared).
- Procurement (Jason) needs the contract redline window to start once the final MAP is accepted. Jason, FYI: Marissa proposes DocuSign after acceptance criteria are confirmed; please confirm if 10 business days is acceptable for procurement review.
- Pilot environment: engineering prefers Redwood Hosted for speed; if the retention/PHI constraints are problematic we’ll move to Dedicated.

Agreed to the acceptance signals as written. A couple of small asks to add to the MAP before we sign off:
- Add a simple example of what a hallucination incident looks like (1–2 example prompts + unacceptable outputs).
- Add contact for incident escalation (pager/email) and expected SLA for remediation (48 hours for pilot-critical issues).

If you can update MAP_v1.xlsx with the incident examples and amendment for DocuSign timing I’ll route to Jason for procurement redlines. Goal: sign and provision week of 2027-03-08 if acceptance checks land on schedule.

Emily Nelson
Head of Clinical Integrations, Clearwell Health
emily.nelson@clearwellhealth.com
